intro: Agent evals are not LLM evals. A correct final answer can ride on a chaotic, expensive, unsafe trajectory. You measure trajectory, not just outcome — task success, tool-call accuracy, step efficiency, cost-per-task, safety violations, robustness to retries. Pair with OpenTelemetry-style observability for runtime visibility.

items.title: Task success
items.whenToUse: The outcome metric. Did the agent achieve the goal?
items.mechanism: Programmatic checks where possible (tests pass, schema matches, exact string). LLM-judge with rubric where not. Calibrate the judge on a human-labeled subset.
items.tradeoff: The only metric stakeholders care about. The most expensive to measure rigorously.

items.title: Trajectory quality
items.whenToUse: Beyond outcome: was the path good? Two agents may both succeed; one took 3 steps, the other 30.
items.mechanism: Trajectory similarity to a reference (Levenshtein over tool-call sequences), intermediate-state checks, LLM-judge on per-step decisions ('would an expert have taken this step?').
items.tradeoff: Catches expensive-but-correct behavior and lucky-but-wrong behavior. Hardest to design rubrics for.

items.title: Tool-call accuracy
items.whenToUse: Specifically scoring whether the right tool was called with the right args.
items.mechanism: Per-step: did the model pick from the right candidate set? Were args schema-valid? Were args semantically correct (e.g. right city looked up)?
items.tradeoff: Cheap to compute on a labeled set. Surfaces bad tool design as much as bad model choice.

items.title: Step efficiency & cost
items.whenToUse: Operational metric. Track per-task: steps taken, tokens in/out, dollars, wall-clock.
items.mechanism: Aggregate per-task from the trace. Compute percentiles (p50, p90, p99). Alert on regressions.
items.tradeoff: The metric most directly tied to whether you can ship the agent.

items.title: Safety & policy violations
items.whenToUse: Whenever the agent has any write tool or user-facing output.
items.mechanism: Programmatic checks for forbidden actions (writes outside allowlist, PII in output). LLM-judge for policy adherence (tone, jailbreak resistance).
items.tradeoff: Compounds with task-success: an answer that violates policy is a failure regardless of correctness.

items.title: Robustness to retries
items.whenToUse: Run the same task N times; how often does it succeed?
items.mechanism: k-shot pass rate, variance across seeds. Catches agents that succeed on average but flake on individual runs.
items.tradeoff: Reveals temperament. Flaky agents are unshippable even at 90% mean success.

items.title: LLM-as-judge — calibrated
items.mechanism: Rubric-driven scoring, low-temperature judge model, two judges with disagreement resolution. Calibrate against human labels on a held-out set. Watch for self-preference (judge prefers its own model family).
items.tradeoff: Cheap and scalable, but it lies in predictable ways. Always validate the judge before trusting it.

items.title: Runtime observability
items.mechanism: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions: spans per agent, per tool, per LLM call. Attributes: tokens, latency, cost. Sinks: Langfuse, LangSmith, Braintrust, Arize, Phoenix, or DIY.
items.tradeoff: Pays for itself the first incident. Skipping it = flying blind.

pitfalls.title: Outcome-only evals
pitfalls.body: If you only measure final-answer accuracy, you can't tell a 30-step correct trajectory from a 3-step one. Both metrics matter; the latter is operationally fatal.

pitfalls.title: Judge self-preference
pitfalls.body: An LLM judge will rate its own model family higher. Use a different model family as judge, or use two judges of different families and require agreement.

pitfalls.title: Eval set of 10 examples
pitfalls.body: Statistically meaningless. Minimum 50 for tracking trends, 200+ for shipping decisions. Stratify by sub-task.

pitfalls.title: Evals not gating deploy
pitfalls.body: Evals you don't run before deploy are documentation, not safety. Wire them into CI; fail the deploy on regression.

pitfalls.title: Eval set in training data
pitfalls.body: If your model was trained on the eval, the score is meaningless. Hold out a private set and refresh quarterly.
